title: HateBench in the Era of Safer LLMs
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the generalizability and robustness of various automated hate speech detectors on LLM-generated hate speech targeting diverse identity groups, including several religious demographics. It measured the rate at which LLMs generate hate speech towards these religious groups under standard and jailbroken conditions, and assessed how effectively commercial and open-source detectors could identify explicit and adversarially perturbed religious hate speech.
findings: Religion was the identity category with the highest proportion of hate samples generated by the evaluated LLMs, with hate speech shares per religious group ranging between approximately 49% and 55%. This confirms findings from the original HateBench paper that religious identities are particularly targeted in LLM-generated hate speech. The automated hate speech detectors generally maintained high F1-scores (over 0.8) for explicit hate speech targeting religious groups such as Christians, Hindus, and Mormons, but performed slightly worse for the Atheist category.
